lessons.title: Everything is a file; the shell
lessons.body: Files, devices, even processes appear under the filesystem. The shell (bash/zsh) glues small tools with pipes: `cmd1 | cmd2` feeds one's output into the next. Core tools: ls, cd, cat, less, grep (search), find (locate files), awk/cut (columns), sort, uniq, wc. Learning to chain these is 80% of day-to-day Linux and log analysis.

lessons.title: Permissions and users
lessons.body: Each file has an owner, a group, and rwx bits for owner/group/other (e.g. 0640). root (uid 0) can do anything. sudo runs one command as root. Least privilege on Linux = correct ownership and mode, plus not running as root. SUID binaries run as their owner regardless of who launches them - a classic privilege-escalation hunting ground.

lessons.title: Processes and networking from the shell
lessons.body: ps/top show processes; kill sends signals. ss -tulpn shows listening sockets and the program behind each port - the Linux answer to 'what's exposed on this box'. systemctl manages services (the systemd equivalent of Windows services). Logs live in journalctl and /var/log.

quiz.q: Which command shows listening ports and their programs?
quiz.why: ss -tulpn: TCP/UDP listening sockets with PID/program.
It runs as its owner - why misconfigured SUID is a privesc path.

quiz.q: What does `grep error app.log | wc -l` do?
quiz.why: grep filters to matching lines, wc -l counts them.
